newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: German court rules in favour of Akzo unit.
newsitem.headline: German court rules in favour of Akzo unit.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Wednesday that a German court ruled in favour of its unit Organon Teknika in a patent dispute with Hoffmann-La Roche.

"Organon Teknika neither directly nor indirectly infringes in a nucleic acid amplification patent owned by Swiss healthcare company Hoffmann-La Roche, the District court of Dusseldorf ruled on October 1," a statement said.
Organon Teknika manufactures and sells diagnostic tests for HIV, the Aids virus, which are based on its patented Nasba nucleic acid amplification technology.
Hoffmann-La Roche had alleged that the Nasba technology infringes its patents in its PCR amplification technology.
According to the Dusseldorf Court, the Nasba process is fundamentally different from the procedure protected by the Hoffmann-La Roche patents.
"Nor do the Nasba test kits from Organon Teknika infringe the patents, because patent protection can only extend to kits suitable to the patented process," the statement said.
This ruling confirms earlier judgements in the Netherlands by the District Court and the Appeal Court, in The Hague.
